idiom-31-q56.truthCondition: Two market chefs repeatedly argue angrily about who gets to use their shared oven first.
idiom-31-q56.correctReason: 正確句把慣用語用於兩名廚師反覆激烈爭執，並保留共用焗爐的使用次序。

foils.text: The two market chefs keep fighting like cat and dog over who should clean the shared oven.
foils.reason: 「clean」把爭議由誰先使用焗爐改成誰負責清潔。

foils.text: The two market chefs fought like cat and dog only once over the shared oven.
foils.reason: 「only once」把不斷爭吵改成單次爭執。

foils.text: The two market chefs take turns using the shared oven without arguing.
foils.reason: 「without arguing」把激烈爭執改成和平輪流。

idiom-31-q57.truthCondition: Every time the morning programme changes its script, its two presenters start another fierce argument.
idiom-31-q57.correctReason: 「whenever」保留節目每次改稿就觸發兩名主持人再次激烈爭吵的關係。

foils.text: The two presenters fight like cat and dog whenever the morning programme keeps its original script.
foils.reason: 「keeps its original script」把觸發情況由改稿改成沒有改稿。

foils.text: The two presenters fought like cat and dog only once when the morning programme changed its script.
foils.reason: 「only once」把每次改稿都會吵改成只吵過一次。

foils.text: The two presenters calmly agree whenever the morning programme changes its script.
foils.reason: 「calmly agree」把每次改稿便激烈爭吵改成平靜達成共識。

idiom-31-q58.truthCondition: Two rowing coaches used to argue furiously over training plans, but now decide together.
idiom-31-q58.correctReason: 「used to」把激烈爭吵放在過去；正確句保留現在共同決定訓練事項的轉變。

foils.text: The two rowing coaches still fight like cat and dog over training plans, although they decide together now.
foils.reason: 「still」說現在仍激烈爭吵；原題說現在會共同作決定，不再是以往的爭吵模式。

foils.text: The two rowing coaches used to fight like cat and dog over race results, but they now decide together.
foils.reason: 「race results」把昔日爭議由訓練計劃改成比賽成績。

foils.text: The two rowing coaches used to decide together, but now fight like cat and dog over training plans.
foils.reason: 這句把以前爭吵、現在共同決定的時間線倒轉。

idiom-31-q59.truthCondition: The two leaders of a book drive argue angrily every time they schedule a collection day.
idiom-31-q59.correctReason: 正確句保留圖書募捐活動的兩名負責人，每次安排收書日期便激烈爭吵。

foils.text: The two book-drive leaders fight like cat and dog whenever they select books for donation.
foils.reason: 「select books」把爭議由收書日期改成挑選捐贈書籍。

foils.text: The two book-drive leaders fought like cat and dog once when planning a collection day.
foils.reason: 「once」把每次安排日期都吵改成只吵一次。

foils.text: The two book-drive leaders agree peacefully whenever they plan a collection day.
foils.reason: 「agree peacefully」把每次激烈爭吵改成和平同意。

idiom-31-q60.truthCondition: The café co-owners may resume their frequent angry arguments if forced to share one tiny counter again.
idiom-31-q60.correctReason: 「may ... again」保留可能重現的舊有爭吵；條件是再次共用狹小櫃檯。

foils.text: The two café co-owners may fight like cat and dog again if each gets a separate counter.
foils.reason: 「each gets a separate counter」把條件由共用小櫃檯改成各有櫃檯。

foils.text: The two café co-owners will certainly fight like cat and dog again if they share one tiny counter.
foils.reason: 「will certainly」把原題的可能重現改成必然發生。

foils.text: The two café co-owners may work peacefully again if they have to share one tiny counter.
foils.reason: 「work peacefully」把可能再起的激烈爭吵改成可能和平合作。
